request.instructions:
You audit the close of a design session for 3D printing in OpenSCAD. You get the user's REQUEST. The harness verified the final version of the design and gives you, in JSON, what it measured (VERIFIED) and the spec adjustments it detected: changes of the spec towards what the mesh already measured, without the part changing (ADJUSTMENTS). Read the designer's CLOSE and answer only with a JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"unsupported": [{"claim": "...", "reason": "..."}], "untold_adjustments": [{"adjustment": "...", "reason": "..."}], "unmeasured": [{"requirement": "...", "how": "..."}]}
- unsupported: every claim the close presents as verified (measured, checked, that it meets, that it fits, that it does not collide, that it goes in, that it prints without supports) that VERIFIED does not back: it is not there, it says something else or the numbers do not match. Leave out: what the close states as not verified, an opinion, an intention, or a description of the design that does not claim to have been checked.
- untold_adjustments: every part of ADJUSTMENTS whose adjustments the close does not mention with their reason (one mention per part saying what was adjusted and why is enough).
- unmeasured: every requirement of the REQUEST about how the product moves or what it fits that VERIFIED does not show measured (the close leaves it not verified, or leaves it out), when one of these declarations has the harness measure it; "how" names it: stops (a part that stops a motion at an end of its range: a drawer that does not come out, a hinge that opens to 110°, the way a ratchet does not turn), rests (a detent that holds a motion at given positions: a lid that clicks at each step), flex (a snap or a detent that bends while a part moves or as it goes in), held (a part that must not come off the assembled product), screw (a thread), drives (gears or a rack that turn each other), print_in_place (a product printed already assembled), standard (the fit of one of these four bought parts, and no other: a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B board, a 608 bearing, an AA cell, an M3 nut). Leave out sizes, walls, holes and other features (the designer's own spec measures those), a part that must not move at all, and what no declaration measures (strength, stiffness, feel, friction, wear, looks, the material, the printer).
Empty lists if there is nothing to object to. Be precise: quote the claim as it is written.

REQUEST
# Gridfinity bin, 2 x 1

A storage bin for my Gridfinity drawer system, 2 units by 1 unit and 3 units tall.

- The Gridfinity grid is 42 mm per unit, so the bin's outside is 83.5 x 41.5 mm (0.25 mm of
  clearance on each side); height units are 7 mm.
- The standard Gridfinity foot under each unit, so it drops into a standard baseplate: the
  stepped profile of 0.8 mm at 45 degrees, 1.8 mm vertical and 2.15 mm at 45 degrees.
- The standard stacking lip on top, so another bin stacks on it.
- A label shelf along one long side, and a scoop at the front so small parts slide out.
- PLA on a Bambu Lab A1 with a 0.4 mm nozzle, no supports.

Show me the bin.

Here is the bin.

Verified:
- Outside 83.5 x 41.5 x 21.0 mm fills its box exactly [[default output]]; one watertight body, 0 bad edges, 0 inverted shells, volume 25137.6 mm3, 0 through holes [[G2]] — single-part bin so no assembly is required [[G3]] [[G4]].
- Prints flat on its foot bottoms: bed support face 2534.7 mm2 at z=0 [[bed]], part rests on minimum z, no bodies starting in air, fits Bambu Lab A1 with 86.25 / 107.25 / 235.0 mm margins [[G5]].
- Standard Gridfinity feet under each unit: left and right foot bottom boxes 100% material [[foot_left]] [[foot_right]], foot profile seen up close [[foot_profile]].
- Only overhangs are inside declared zones, declared coverage 28.11%, no bridge over 10 mm [[G5]].
- Top stacking lip, 100% material [[stack_lip]], seen up close [[lip_view]].
- Label shelf along +Y, 100% material [[label_shelf]], seen up close [[label_view]].
- Front scoop cut through +X wall, void box 100% empty [[scoop_void]], seen up close [[scoop_view]].
- Walls 1.6 mm [[wall_side]] and 6.0 mm floor [[floor]] measured by thickness rays.
- Compiles with no warnings or errors [[G1]] and mesh meets the full spec [[G7]].

Not verified:
- Fit in a real baseplate, stacking feel with another bin, label adhesion on the shelf slope, and how clean the scoop surface prints in PLA on a 0.4 mm nozzle — geometry only, depends on printer and material.
- Exact foot segment heights and taper angles, lip inset dimension, shelf angle and scoop radius were not separately measured; only material presence, void emptiness and close views listed above were verified.
- Spec adjustment: the side-wall thickness probe was moved from z=10 to z=16. At z=10 the inward ray crosses the label-shelf wedge, measuring about 4.5 mm instead of 1.6 mm; the wall itself was unchanged. The original probe point was badly posed against the requested shelf, so the spec was moved to measure clear wall above the shelf.
